title: LINQ Query Expression Syntax
description: Learn the SQL-like query syntax for writing LINQ queries in C#.

data.text: There are two basic ways to write a LINQ query for `IEnumerable` collections or `IQueryable` data sources:

items: **Method Syntax** (Method Extension Syntax / Fluent) — Extension methods

data.text: Query syntax is similar to SQL (Structured Query Language) used for databases. It is defined directly within C# code.

data.title: Query Syntax Structure
data.content: The basic structure of a LINQ query
data.code:
from <range variable> in <collection>
<Standard Query Operators> <lambda expression>
<select or groupBy operator> <result formation>

data.caption: Structure of a LINQ query expression

    A[from clause] --> B[Range variable]

data.text: Query syntax starts with a `from` clause followed by a range variable. The `from` clause is structured like `from rangeVariableName in IEnumerableCollection`. In English, this means "from each object in the collection". It is similar to a `foreach` loop: `foreach(Student s in studentList)`.
After the `from` clause, you can use different Standard Query Operators to filter, group, or join elements of the collection. There are around 50 Standard Query Operators available in LINQ.
LINQ query syntax always ends with a `Select` or `Group` clause. The `Select` clause is used to shape the data. You can select the whole object as it is or only some properties of it.

terms.definition: The variable in the from clause that represents each element in the collection, similar to the iteration variable in a foreach loop.
Specifies the data source and range variable. Must be the first clause in a query expression.
Filters elements based on a condition. Similar to SQL WHERE.
Shapes the result data. Must be the last clause in a query expression.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Query syntax is similar to SQL and is defined within C# code
Queries start with 'from' and end with 'select' or 'group by'
The range variable represents each element in the collection
Query syntax is converted to method syntax at compile time
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn the method syntax (fluent syntax) for LINQ queries.
